post.caption: Celluloid plastic could pass for ivory. It is often called the first commercially successful plastic. It was made from nitrocellulose softened with camphor. It is credited to John Wesley Hyatt, a printer by trade. It copied costly materials like ivory and coral. By the 1880s, fake tortoiseshell combs were selling well. Ivory look pieces were often sold as French Ivory. In 1878, Hyatt got a US patent for making combs from celluloid. It made look alikes of fine goods affordable to many. In the 1920s, DuPont sold celluloid dresser sets as Pyralin. Around 1900, celluloid also gave ping pong balls their bounce.
